clue.text: Cinders in carriage is making a great show

indicators.note: in tells us the cinders sit inside the vehicle named

parts.note: a fly is a light one-horse hired carriage
ash is what remains after burning, cinders

explanation.surface: Cinderella arriving at the ball in her coach causes quite a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' looks like Cinderella, whose coach is the carriage, but here it just means ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showy and ostentatious makes a great show, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Preserving a reputation, which spendthrift never can do?

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: a spendthrift cannot face up to putting money aside

explanation.surface: Keeping a good name is beyond a waster.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the compound: one who spends freely never can face saving money.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting to avoid embarrassment or loss of dignity is the standard sense of the hyphenated term.

clue.text: Corrupt US political party stripped Arab capital

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are removed

parts.note: Tammany Hall was the notoriously corrupt Democratic machine in New York

explanation.surface: A corrupt American party stripped an Arab capital of its assets.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan, an Arab nation.

clue.text: Husband calm about wife making an entrance

indicators.note: about tells us the calming word goes round the letter for wife

parts.note: to allay is to calm or soothe

explanation.surface: A husband soothes his wife as he makes his entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage just inside the front door, an entrance hall, is one.

clue.text: Nearly went wrong on role in The Knot Garden?

indicators.note: on places the shortened error word straight after the role word

parts.note: a part is an actor's role

indicators.note: nearly means stopping just short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: erred means made a mistake, went wrong

explanation.surface: An opera singer nearly fluffs a role in Tippett's opera The Knot Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knot Garden is Michael Tippett's opera, which sends the mind to the stage; the question mark marks a knot garden as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot garden is a formal bed laid out in intricate patterns, an example of an ornamental flower garden of this kind.

clue.text: Bulk transporter must be very cold — minus Celsius

indicators.note: minus means the temperature letter is taken away

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold

explanation.surface: A lorry hauling freight must be freezing, with temperatures below zero Celsius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus' looks like a sub-zero temperature but is the deletion signal. An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry, a tractor unit pulling a trailer, carries heavy freight.

clue.text: Trial complete about universal protection for soldiers

indicators.note: about places the two words around the letter for universal

parts.note: a test is a trial
to do a task is to complete it
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A trial complete, soldiers get universal protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman testudo was a tortoise formation of interlocked shields shielding legionaries.

clue.text: Gorgeous gunners leaving without a note

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

indicators.note: without means the next letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: vanishing means disappearing, leaving

explanation.surface: The artillerymen are leaving without a word, looking splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravishing is stunningly beautiful, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Pocket needs repairing regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trouser pocket in need of mending now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money is to gain or take it, as wages.

clue.text: Devotee of album that is keeping LP spinning

parts.note: a disc is a record album

indicators.note: keeping means holding the reversed record inside

parts.note: IE abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: spinning turns the two letters round

explanation.surface: A fan of an album keeps an LP spinning on the turntable.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a teacher, faith or idea is a devotee of it.

clue.text: Cooperative somewhere along the line turning to AI for beef

indicators.note: somewhere along the line says the change happens at some point within the word
turning to says one pair of letters becomes another, the pair printed next

parts.note: compliant means willing to go along, cooperative

explanation.surface: A cooperative farm somewhere along a railway switches to artificial insemination, prompting grumbles about beef.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters IA in the middle of the cooperative word swap to AI, as 'turning to AI' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a grievance or grumble, as in 'what's your beef?'

clue.text: Cut off town finally swept away in river

indicators.note: swept away means a letter is carried off out of the river's name

parts.note: the Severn is Britain's longest river

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of town

explanation.surface: A town is cut off when the river floods and sweeps things away.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to cut it off or separate it.

clue.text: Method of learning way round to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with puts the round word at the front of the charade

parts.note: a round is a sandwich made from two slices of bread
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: A teaching method that goes the long way round at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich course alternates periods of college study with work placements, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of vocational study alternating classroom terms with industrial experience, so a method of learning.

clue.text: Before start of Thermopylae the whole Greek city cheers

indicators.note: before puts the city ahead of the opening letter

parts.note: all means the whole
Thebes is an ancient city of Boeotia in Greece

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Greek soldiers cheer one another on before the battle of Thermopylae.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewell or toast formulas wishing someone good fortune.

clue.text: Civic hydro's built in a French town

indicators.note: built in says the town lies inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A spa town's civic hydro, a hydropathic establishment, has been built in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Vichy is a spa town in central France, famed for its waters.

clue.text: Anglo-French project missing out English: a time for treaty

indicators.note: missing out means leaving a letter out

parts.note: Concorde was the supersonic airliner built by Britain and France

explanation.surface: An Anglo-French scheme leaves out the English, a time for treaty talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Queen beheaded in place of shots, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the headless queen inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation of place in street addresses

indicators.note: beheaded says the first letter comes off

parts.note: Victoria was queen of Britain 1837-1901

explanation.surface: A queen is beheaded in a place where shots are fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' suggests gunfire, but here they are photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictorial means made of pictures, and shots, perhaps, are photographs.

clue.text: What will strain company leading potential mission to Mars

indicators.note: leading puts the company abbreviation in front

parts.note: a lander is a craft designed to touch down on a planet

explanation.surface: A firm heads a planned Mars mission that will be a strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests stress, but here means sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl for draining or sieving food.

clue.text: Matchless? Not so —— plainer, unfortunately

parts.note: no is a flat denial, not so

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the word plainer has gone awry and is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something matchless? Not so; it is plainer, sad to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash simply joins NO to the anagram of PLAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrivalled, without equal, is matchless; the word is also a noun for a peerless person.

clue.text: One giving performance rates it poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are arranged badly and need reordering

explanation.surface: A performer rates their own act badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Coastal curve where wreck's getting left to vanish

indicators.note: to vanish says that letter disappears from the word

parts.note: to blight is to spoil or wreck

explanation.surface: A bay where a shipwreck has been left to disappear beneath the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a long gentle bend in a coastline, forming a wide bay.

clue.text: Sheriff's man hit when containing trouble

indicators.note: containing means the blow word holds the trouble word inside

parts.note: biff is a punch, a hit
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A sheriff's officer lashes out when facing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is an officer under the sheriff who serves writs and seizes goods.

clue.text: Suggest not using school tart's return in short story

indicators.note: in puts the school and the reversed sharp word inside the story

parts.note: a conte is a short story, especially in French literature
to train is to school or teach

indicators.note: return asks for the tart word read backwards

parts.note: acid means sour or tart

explanation.surface: A short story in which a schoolgirl's tart remark comes back to bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically, a factor that contraindicates a drug signals it should not be used.

clue.text: Jelly with a lot of flavour

indicators.note: a lot of means most, but not all, of the word

parts.note: spice is flavour or seasoning

explanation.surface: A jelly with a strong taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock.

clue.text: Endure an attempt on Egypt's leader

indicators.note: on puts the leader's letter after the attempt

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
a bid is an attempt

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Holding firm against a coup attempt on Egypt's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to bear or tolerate it.

clue.text: Fellow takes one for a shot at golf

indicators.note: takes ... for means the next letter is swapped in for one already there
for marks the letter being replaced in the fellow word

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man takes a single swing at golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes one for' puts I where the A of CHAP was.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a short lofted stroke onto the green.

clue.text: Pluto's sphere underwent outer space spinning

parts.note: had means experienced, underwent

indicators.note: spinning means the pair of letters turns round
outer picks the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The dwarf planet Pluto has been spinning through outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer space' gives SE, which 'spinning' turns to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the Roman god of the underworld, so his domain is the realm of the dead.

clue.text: When rupee fails, a couple of prices unexpectedly drop

indicators.note: fails says the currency letter drops out of the mix
unexpectedly signals the remaining letters are jumbled
a couple of means two copies of the price word

parts.note: price is the singular of prices, taken twice
R is the abbreviation for the rupee

explanation.surface: When the Indian currency collapses, prices take a sudden fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Two PRICEs, with R removed ('fails'), are rearranged ('unexpectedly').
explanation.definitionFit: A precipice is a sheer cliff face, a steep drop.

clue.text: Nice tape playing operetta

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A good tape is playing a light opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of 1881 bears this title, an example of an operetta.

clue.text: Pretend to have influence

definitions.meaning: to put on or feign, as in putting on an accent
to act upon or alter something

explanation.surface: Pretending to have power over others.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to the verb: to feign a manner, and to make a difference to something.
